extracted.intended_audience: patent and trademark attorneys, agents, and IP practitioners working in or with Ecuadorian IP law
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on prosecution, substantive requirements, and litigation procedures for patents and trademarks under Ecuadorian law and Decision 486 (Andean Community). Covers filing formalities, patentability criteria, oppositions, remedies, and enforcement practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Within six months from the date of publication of the application, the applicant must request examination to determine whether the application is patentable; if not requested the application shall be considered abandoned. (Art. 44 of Decision 486).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For such examination the Patent Office may request reports from experts or from scientific or technological bodies and may inquire of competent national offices of other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action response timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If during the examination it is found that the application does not meet any of the requirements, the Patent Office will notify the applicant and within a period of sixty days from the notification a response must be filed; this period may be extended once for thirty additional days. If no response or inadequate response is given, the patent will be denied. (Art. 45 Decision 486).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall be granted to all inventions, being of products or processes, in all fields of technology, if the invention is new, involves an inventive level and is susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness to a person skilled in art), and industrial application (may be produced or used in productive activity including services) are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs and utility models definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial design: particular appearance of a product resulting from arrangement of lines, colors, two- or three-dimensional outward shape, texture or material without changing intended use. Utility model: new form, configuration or arrangement of components that allows better or different operation, use or manufacture and lacks sufficient inventive level for a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software protection rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer programs are protected as Copyright; however, if the computer program or software is part of an industrially applicable invention, then the software will be protected as a part in the patent of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to articles 104 and 131 of the Organic Code for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush claims not allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 30 states that claims must specify the subject matter for which patent protection is sought; they must be stated clearly and concisely and be fully substantiated by the description. Markush claims are not allowable in Ecuador.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological material deposit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention involves biological material and the invention cannot be carried out from the description, it must be accompanied by a deposit of the material by the filing date (or priority date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits with international authorities recognized under the 1977 Budapest Treaty or other institutions acknowledged by the competent national office are valid. Include depositary name and address, date of deposit, and assigned number. Deposit must allow interested persons to obtain samples by the date of expiration of the period stipulated in article 40.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Orange-Book-style linkage system
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no US-style Orange Book linkage system available in Ecuador.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling rules (Presidential Decree No. 522/2015) depend on patent status for pharmaceuticals (e.g., designation 'Generic Medicine' if patent expired).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims clarity and substantiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall specify the subject matter for which patent protection is sought; must be clear, concise and fully substantiated by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims may be independent or dependent; multiple dependent claims allowed (referring to two or more previous claims). For method/process claims, the inventive step should be well defined and characterized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, inventive step and industrial application definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty: not in the prior art. Inventive level: would not have been obvious or obviously derived from prior art to a person skilled in the technical field. Industrial application: subject matter may be produced or used in any productive activity, including services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application formalities and sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: With the application the applicant must submit title/name of invention, description, a summary, one or more claims, necessary plans and drawings; when biological material is involved, a deposit. The description must be sufficiently clear and complete to allow a person skilled in the art to execute it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also require payment voucher of fees (article 280 of new Ecuadorian IP Law).

rubrics_metrics.name: SME fee reductions eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A discount of 90% applies to all official fees for patent procedures and maintenance for small and medium enterprises (PYMES), legally recognized universities, independent inventors, public institutions, small and medium farmers, and businesses of popular and solidarity economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: An extract of the application is published; within a 60-day term after publication, whoever has a legitimate interest can file an opposition. If an opposition is filed, the National Office notifies the applicant giving term to respond in the following 60 days after notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions and responses interact with the substantive examination and may be considered in the 6-month window to request examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner interviews practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner interviews are allowed but are an accustomed practice rather than a formal part of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection provided by pending patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights are only enforceable once the patent has been granted by the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents have a term of twenty years counted from the filing date of the corresponding application in the Member Country.

rubrics_metrics.name: No expedited examination currently available
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to expedite examination. Ecuador is negotiating a Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) with some South American countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendments restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request modification of the application at any time during registration, but the modification may not involve extending the scope of protection beyond the use indicated in the initial application; correction of material errors allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims can be amended when answering official actions or third-party oppositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may divide their applications into two or more divisional applications at any time during processing, but none may extend the scope of protection beyond the initial application; divisional keeps original filing date or initial priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The national office may request division if unity of invention requirement is not met; priorities for partial/multiple priorities must be stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: No provisional application; certificate of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provisional application under Ecuadorian law; however, an inventor may apply for a certificate of protection for one year preceding the patent application which grants right of priority to submit the patent application within the following year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting patent infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent confers exclusive rights to exploit the invention and to prevent third parties from: (a) manufacture the patented product; (b) offer for sale, sell or use the patented, imported, or stored product; (c) employ the patented procedure; (d) perform acts a/b with products obtained directly through the patented procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defenses and exceptions to patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent holder may not exercise rights when: (a) use is private and non-commercial; (b) use is non-profit, experimental, academic or scientific; (c) acts contained in article 5 of the Paris Convention apply; (d) using patented biological material as initial basis for obtaining new viable material, unless repeated use required; (e) importation of patented product placed into trade in any country with consent of titleholder or licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural enforcement options (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Available administrative and jurisdictional actions; the most effective way for a patent owner to enforce rights in Ecuador is through administrative protection of industrial property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative stage handled by National Director of Industrial Property and appeals to the Intellectual Property Committee; jurisdictional courts handle civil/criminal as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to sue for infringement (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal standing is limited to the titleholder; if patent holder has not filed an infringement action, a potential infringer could request a negative enforcement action to declare its conduct does not infringe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative vs jurisdictional courts (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage enforcement: Administrative Stage (National Director of Industrial Property; appeals to Intellectual Property Committee) and Jurisdictional Stage (competent judge of the defendant's location or where infringement has effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect medium-high expertise at administrative stage and low expertise at jurisdictional stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte remedies and injunctive relief (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex-parte remedies are effective to stop infringement. Authority can order seizure and deposit of merchandise and other objects violating IP rights and temporary closure of the offender's establishment when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated litigation timelines (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time to reach a first instance decision in an administrative stage is 5 to 6 years. Preliminary injunctions may be confirmed or revoked in the final resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of limitations for infringement claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limit for seeking a remedy for patent infringement is 2 years counted from the date the patent holder had knowledge of the infringement or, in any case, 5 years counted from the date the last act of infringement occurred. (Article 244 Decision 486).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and standing for patent invalidity (reconsideration/nullity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration to nullify registration can be filed if: the subject does not constitute an invention; patent was granted for a non-patentable invention; granted in favor of someone who is not the inventor; a third party in good faith was already manufacturing/using the process before filing; or patent granted with violations of law or on false/erroneous data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standing limited to those who can prove any of the listed cases; invalidity procedure may be bifurcated (infringement before National Direction; invalidity before Committee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-trial discovery and evidence preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Organic Code provides pre-trial discovery and procedures to preserve evidence of infringement or identify the infringer; reports are based on questions or requests made by the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in patent trials
rubrics_metrics.description: In Ecuador, the person who alleges something has to prove what he alleged. Exception: for method patents the burden of proof is reversed onto defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages procedure for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain damages from the losing party you have to initiate an independent civil action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average patent lawsuit costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional fees in a first instance decision may be between US$15,000 to US$20,000 (Ecuador).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier section (trademarks) cited USD15,000–60,000 for some trademark matters over four years; amounts vary with complexity and whether preliminary injunctions reduce costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney fee shifting (patents & trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney fees as set by the national bar are available for the winning parties; the successful litigant may request the judge to order the losing party to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice the amount set by the bar and recognized by judges may not correspond to actual invoiced fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert evidence importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert evidence is critical in any trademark or patent suit; parties may submit their own witnesses and the court may appoint its own. Experts help interpret surveys and controvert positions adopted by the CTO (or comparable authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is typical to submit multiple experts; expert reports help judges resolve cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal liability upon finding of infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no personal liability in patent infringement cases (Ecuador). (By contrast, earlier for trademarks criminal conviction may create personal liability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust/unfair competition considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ecuadorian antitrust law considers any abuse of an intellectual property right to prevail in the market as unfair competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant treaties and laws for trademarks and patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant international instruments include WIPO, TRIPS, Paris Convention, PCT (for patents), NICE (for trademarks), and Decision 486 of the Andean Community; national law is the Organic Code for the Social Knowledge and Innovation Economy (new Ecuadorian IP law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Office must use WIPO’s Andean manual for examination of patents of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of registrable trademarks and non-traditional marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognized signs include nominative, figurative, combined and three-dimensional marks; also sounds, smells, tastes, letters, numbers, colours defined by a shape or combination, product/packaging shape, reliefs, textures, animations, gestures, holograms, and any combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must attach payment voucher and copy of the first application when claiming priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsic distinctiveness criteria (unregisterable signs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs not intrinsically distinctive cannot be registered: signs lacking distinctiveness; usual forms of products/containers; forms imposed by nature or function; forms not offering technical/functional advantage; signs that describe or qualify product features; generic/technical names; common or usual commercial designations; isolated color without specific shape; deceptive signs; reproductions of protected denominations of origin for wines/spirits; imitation of state emblems, official signs, coins, stamps; names of states/local governments; signs contrary to law, morals, public order or decency; signs containing name of protected traditional specialty guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrinsic distinctiveness criteria (likelihood of confusion/dilution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs are not extrinsically distinctive when they are identical or alike so as to provoke confusion with a trademark already applied for or registered for the same or similar products/services, or may cause dilution, unfair advantage, or damage to the titleholder; or identical/similar to protected commercial names, logos, or well-known signs causing confusion or dilution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reproduction/imitation/translation/transliteration of a sign notoriously known, irrespective of goods/services, if it could cause confusion, unfair advantage, or dilution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness/confusing similarity assessment factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctiveness of a trademark is evaluated according to ideological, phonetic and visual elements, considering the products that the trademark identifies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is presumed that confusion exists when dealing with an identical sign to distinguish identical products or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-known and famous mark standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A famous or notoriously known trademark is one well known by the pertinent sector of the consumer public in the country or internationally; a sign of high renown is known by the public in general in the country or abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be submitted to the National Industrial Property Direction and shall comprise a single international class of products or services and contain the required elements (payment voucher, priority documents when applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark opposition procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An extract of the application is published in the Gazette; within 30 days after publication, anyone with a legitimate interest may file an opposition. If filed, the National Office notifies the applicant who has 30 days to respond. After response, application moves to 'registrability' stage for analysis and the authority issues a resolution to grant or deny registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority rights from pending trademark applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a pending application, you have a priority right over applications that are filed after your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical indication definition and reserved use
rubrics_metrics.description: A Geographical Indication identifies a product as original from the territory, region or locality when a determined quality, reputation or characteristic is basically attributable to its geographic origin; use is exclusively reserved to producers, manufacturers and artisans with establishments in the designated locality or region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain name registration restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organic Code prohibits registration, trafficking in, or use of a domain name that is identical or confusingly similar to, or dilutive of, another person’s mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting trademark infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Titleholder may act against others who: use or affix identical or similar trademark on products/services for which the mark is registered; delete or modify the mark for commercial purposes; manufacture labels/packaging reproducing the trademark; use identical or similar signs in commerce for identical or similar goods/services when use may cause confusion or dilution or cause economic/commercial damage; use identical or similar to a well-known mark even for non-commercial public use if it causes dilution or unfair exploitation of prestige.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumption of confusion when identical sign distinguishes identical products/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark enforcement procedure and standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and jurisdictional actions are available; administrative protection is often the most effective. Legal standing is available to any person with a legitimate interest (consumer or titleholder); a potential infringer may request negative enforcement if the titleholder has not sued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court system and judges' expertise (trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Stage: National Director of Industrial Property and appeals to the Intellectual Property Committee; Jurisdictional Stage: competent local judge. Expect high expertise at administrative stage and medium-low expertise at jurisdictional stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated litigation timelines (trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time to reach a first instance decision in an administrative stage is 1 to 2 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner interviews practice (trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner interviews are allowed but are not formally part of the process; they are an accustomed practice.
